base.description: The branch pull requests target and each spec branches from.

branchPrefix.description: Prefix for generated branches, e.g. tagteam/.

conventionsPath.description: A repository document implementers and reviewers are told to read. Null when there is none.

models.description: The $ref is the whole rule here; a keyword placed beside it is discarded.

effort.description: The $ref is the whole rule here; a keyword placed beside it is discarded.

roster.description: Every lens a plan may assign to a spec.

default.description: Lenses applied to every spec unless that spec removes one. A Codex cross-review and the adversary run in addition, always.

verify.description: Commands proving a candidate works. Zero matching commands is reported as not-applicable and waits for a person rather than passing.

when.description: Empty globs and empty keywords mean the command always runs.

ciWaitSec.description: How long to wait for GitHub checks. Still pending at the deadline counts as not-run, which waits for a person. Zero skips CI entirely.

autoMerge.description: When false every pull request waits for approval, whatever the gates say.

setup.description: Commands making a fresh worktree buildable, e.g. npm ci.

copyUntracked.description: Ignored files a build needs, e.g. .env.test. Each must be ignored at its destination or the copy is refused.

reviewExclude.description: Globs whose contents are summarised rather than included in the review diff — lock files, snapshots, generated code.

maxConcurrentCodex.description: How many Codex calls may run at once across this repository.

fixRounds.description: How many rounds of fixes a candidate may take before the spec stops for a person. Each round is followed by a full review panel.

ciRepairs.description: How many times a red pull request may be repaired. Each repair produces a new candidate that runs the whole review cycle again with a fresh fix budget.

planReviewRounds.description: How many rounds of plan review — three readers plus one revision — a goal approval may take.

escalation.description: Raised settings for a ship cycle whose fix rounds have stalled. Null is today's behaviour: every dispatch runs at `models` and `effort`.

after.description: How many fix rounds run at the ordinary settings before the raised ones take over. At least 1: the ordinary settings always get one fix round, and wanting the raised model from the first fix is already expressible by setting `models`/`effort` to it.

models.description: The $ref is the whole rule here; a keyword placed beside it is discarded.

effort.description: The $ref is the whole rule here; a keyword placed beside it is discarded.

plan.description: Settings for the whole of /tagteam:plan, replacing `models` and `effort` there. Null is today's behaviour: every dispatch runs at `models` and `effort`.

models.description: The $ref is the whole rule here; a keyword placed beside it is discarded.

effort.description: The $ref is the whole rule here; a keyword placed beside it is discarded.

roleModels.description: The model each role is dispatched at. Every site carrying a role triple $refs this one, so a role added here is a role added everywhere. Note that `validate-json.mjs` returns on a $ref: a keyword written beside one of those $refs is silently ignored, so anything extra a site needs belongs here instead. Codex model names are not enumerable, which is why `codex` is a non-empty string.

roleEffort.description: The effort each role is dispatched at. Every site carrying a role triple $refs this one, so a role added here is a role added everywhere. Note that `validate-json.mjs` returns on a $ref: a keyword written beside one of those $refs is silently ignored, so anything extra a site needs belongs here instead. The two effort ladders diverge on purpose — the Claude one has `max` and the Codex one does not.
